comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
MEASURED AUDIT before implementation — the gap is TEN methods, not one. This materially widens the
story, so recording it now rather than discovering it mid-flight.

I ran an AST audit over src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/*.py collecting every method invoked on a
'client' or 'transport' receiver, then diffed that set against JiraDataCenterTransport's methods and
against every Protocol declared in _backend.py.

CALLED BY THE CORE, ABSENT FROM THE DC TRANSPORT (10):
    delete_issue, get_comments, get_issue_by_rest, get_issue_links, get_parent_map,
    remove_label, set_entity_property, set_issue_property, set_reporter, validate_assignee_exists

DECLARED ON NO PROTOCOL IN _backend.py — the SAME 10.

All ten ARE implemented for Cloud, spread across adapters/jira/acli_rest.py, acli.py and
acli_graph.py. (My first pass reported three of them as missing from Cloud too; that was wrong — I
had not scanned acli_graph.py. Corrected before recording: Cloud has all ten.)

WHAT THIS MEANS: set_entity_property is not 'the' missing method, it is simply the FIRST one a live
writing pass happened to reach. Nine more sit behind it. Implementing only set_entity_property would
move the crash one call deeper and produce another red CI run — the story would look like progress
while the capability stayed broken.

The TicketTransport Protocol declares six members (create_issue, get_issue, update_issue,
transition_issue_by_name, add_label, search_issues). The core actually calls fifteen. So the port
describes 40% of its own requirement, which is exactly why isinstance conformance, the backend
contract suite, and 1636 reconciler unit tests were all green against a transport that cannot
complete a writing pass.

IMPLICATION FOR THIS STORY'S SHAPE, for the reviewer: the third AC (the structural audit test) is now
the load-bearing one, not a nicety — it is what converts 'I found ten' into 'the eleventh cannot be
introduced silently'. And the live tests are the only oracle that can confirm the set is actually
complete, since the audit proves what the core calls STATICALLY and cannot prove which paths a real
pass exercises.

Some of the ten may be reachable only on paths a DC deployment never takes; that is a judgement to
make per method WITH evidence, not an assumption. Whatever is deliberately left unimplemented should
raise a clear NotImplementedError naming the DC limitation rather than AttributeError mid-pass.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PLAN CORRECTED after review-plan BLOCKED with three findings. All three were right, and TWO of them
corrected MY OWN audit — which is the useful part of this entry.

BLOCK 1 (COH/E1) — the Scope section still said 'implement set_entity_property' while the Approach
section explicitly REJECTED the single-method fix and AC1 demanded all of them. An implementer reading
Scope alone would have done exactly the thing the plan argues against. My earlier edit updated
Context/Approach/ACs and missed Scope. Fixed, and the stale counts elsewhere ('nine more', 'the core
calls fifteen', 'I found ten') are now consistent too.

BLOCK 2 (E4) — I claimed a blanket 'no member may be absent, so no call site can fail with
AttributeError'. Wrong for get_parent_map: fetcher.py:448 reads
'if project_key and hasattr(client, "get_parent_map")', so its absence degrades to an empty parent
map rather than crashing. Verified by reading the line. It is still a real gap — DC silently loses
inbound parent relationships — but it is a FUNCTIONAL gap needing a deliberate decision, not an
AttributeError fix, and the plan now separates the two categories with its own AC.

BLOCK 3 (G6) — the reviewer found delete_issue_link (dispatch_one.py:731), which my audit MISSED.
Diagnosing why mattered more than adding it: my AST pattern matched only 'client.method(...)' CALL
forms, but the reconciler routinely passes the method as a VALUE —
'_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)'. set_entity_property itself is called that way
at dispatch_one.py:321 and I only caught it because it ALSO appears in call form at
binding_store.py:517. Pure luck.

Re-ran the audit collecting EVERY attribute access on a client/transport receiver, not just calls.
That found delete_issue_link AND a second one nobody had spotted: set_parent (dispatch_one.py:544).

CORRECTED FIGURES: the core reaches for 21 distinct transport members; TWELVE are absent from
JiraDataCenterTransport (was 'ten'). Eleven are unguarded and would raise AttributeError; get_parent_map
is the lone hasattr-guarded one. All twelve exist for Cloud.

THE LESSON, worth carrying: a static audit is only as good as its match pattern, and a narrow pattern
fails SILENTLY — it returns a confident, wrong, smaller number. I had already published 'ten' as a
measured fact before the reviewer disproved it. Measurement is not automatically evidence; the
measuring instrument needs checking too.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PLAN CORRECTED A SECOND TIME. Review #2 BLOCKED with four findings; all four were right, and the most
important one INVERTS this story's framing.

FINDING: my proposed enforcement mechanism could not work. I wrote that a transport missing a member
should 'fail an isinstance check at construction'. But TicketTransport is declared
'class TicketTransport(Protocol)' with NO @runtime_checkable — so isinstance against it raises
TypeError rather than returning False. Verified directly:

    TypeError: Instance and class checks can only be used with @runtime_checkable protocols

I had assumed it was runtime_checkable because Backend and the capability protocols are. The plan now
adds the decorator explicitly and names WHERE the assertion runs (the backend factories), which was
the separate COH/E1 finding — the AC promised a construction-time check that no section located.

THE BIG ONE: 'eleven would raise AttributeError' was FACTUALLY WRONG, and wrong in the direction that
matters. I classified every call site by whether an enclosing try swallows Exception:

    propagates (crashes):        2   get_issue_by_rest, set_reporter
    swallowed at EVERY site:     7   delete_issue_link, get_comments, get_issue_links,
                                     set_issue_property, set_parent, validate_assignee_exists,
                                     get_parent_map (hasattr-guarded)
    MIXED (crash some, swallowed elsewhere): 3   delete_issue, remove_label, set_entity_property

So a DC deployment does NOT mostly crash. It mostly APPEARS TO CONVERGE while quietly not syncing
comments, links, parents, issue properties, or validating assignees. set_entity_property is swallowed
at 2 of its 3 sites and crashes at the third — which is the ONLY reason any of this was ever
discovered. The crash was the LUCKY case.

CONSEQUENCE, and why this changes the story rather than just correcting a number: 'no AttributeError'
is the WRONG acceptance bar. It is already true at most sites, and true for the wrong reason. Fixing
only the crash would yield a GREEN live run with every silent gap intact — strictly worse than today,
because the green run would then be read as proof the capability works. The ACs now require asserting
each member is PRESENT, not merely that nothing raised.

That is the same trap as the completion-verifier lesson from earlier this session and the
half-fix landmine in J7: an absence of errors is not evidence of function. Three times now this epic
has produced a variant of it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PLAN CORRECTED A THIRD TIME. Review #3 BLOCKED with three findings, all verified in source. They
change this story from 'translate twelve methods' to 'TRIAGE twelve methods', which is a different
job.

1. get_parent_map — COPYING CLOUD WOULD BREAK. acli_graph.py:180 uses POST /rest/api/3/search/jql with
   an opaque nextPageToken CURSOR, and its own docstring records (ticket 8b25, live-proven) that the
   legacy /rest/api/3/search is RETIRED at HTTP 410 and that sending startAt is REJECTED with HTTP
   400. That endpoint and pagination model are Cloud-v3 only; DC v2 has POST /rest/api/2/search with
   OFFSET paging. So my Approach instruction to 'read each Cloud counterpart first' was actively
   misleading for this method — following it yields a 404/400 against DC. Needs a fresh v2
   implementation.

2. set_reporter — UNREACHABLE ON DC, so implementing it would be DEAD CODE. Its only call site,
   dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_apply_reporter, resolves via _jira_account_id_for ->
   identity.jira_account_id and on None records an 'outbound-reporter-unresolved' alert and RETURNS
   before client.set_reporter is ever invoked. DC has no accountIds at all (NameIdentity keys on
   name), so that resolution always misses. The real decision is UPSTREAM — teach the call site DC's
   name identity, or record reporter sync as unsupported on DC.

   Note this also corrects MY OWN classification from the previous round: I had set_reporter in the
   'propagates (crashes)' bucket. It cannot crash on DC because it is never called. That is a THIRD
   failure category I did not have — unreachable-by-call-site — alongside crash and silent
   degradation.

3. (same root as 1 — the pagination incompatibility, stated separately.)

The plan now requires a RECORDED VERDICT per member (IMPLEMENT with the DC v2 shape / NOT-APPLICABLE
via NotImplementedError / UNREACHABLE-BY-CALL-SITE with the upstream decision named), each backed by
call-site evidence rather than by symmetry with Cloud. Two new ACs cover get_parent_map's v2
pagination and set_reporter's upstream decision specifically.

RUNNING TALLY of what the reviewer has corrected in my measurements across three rounds: the count
(ten -> twelve), the failure mode (mostly-crashes -> mostly-silent), the enforcement mechanism
(isinstance, which raises TypeError on a non-runtime_checkable Protocol), and now the portability
assumption (Cloud's implementation is not a template). Every correction made the picture worse and
the plan better. I am recording that pattern deliberately: my audits have been confidently wrong
three times in a row, and the common thread is that I measured STRUCTURE (what exists, what is
called) without checking SEMANTICS (whether it is reachable, whether the endpoint transfers).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
UPSTREAM DECISION RESOLVED — set_reporter. The plan offered a binary (teach the call site DC's name
identity, OR declare reporter sync unsupported). Both were wrong. The evidence gives a three-part
answer, and one part is a defect neither the plan nor the reviewer had.

(1) THE CALL SITE NEEDS NO CHANGE — my own J7 fix already did that work.
    jira_account_id (identity.py:224) resolves an identity and returns its {provider:'jira'}
    external_id. Since [rebar:5f48-244c-7063-42d0] merged, DC ghost identities are minted under
    provider 'jira' with external_id = the DC USERNAME. Measured on a scratch repo after minting a DC
    identity:
        jira_account_id('1bb8-9d6a-dee5-46b5') -> 'dcuser'     # identity TICKET ID
        jira_account_id('dcuser')              -> None          # bare username
        jira_account_id('DC User')             -> None          # display name
        jira_account_id('dcuser@example.com')  -> None          # email
    So the seam is already vendor-neutral: it hands back whatever external_id the FAMILY stored, which
    for DC is the username — exactly the value DC's REST needs. set_reporter is therefore NOT
    unreachable; it is CONDITIONALLY reachable, on tickets whose reporter field holds an identity id.
    The reviewer's 'unreachable' verdict was correct for the tree it read; the merged J7 fix changed
    it underneath. dispatch_apply_phases.py comes OFF the scope list.

(2) THE TRANSPORT METHOD IS NEEDED, with a DC payload. Cloud PUTs reporter.accountId; DC has no
    accountId at all, so DC must PUT {'fields': {'reporter': {'name': <username>}}}. Note the local
    variable is called account_id at the call site and will hold a USERNAME on DC — functionally
    correct, misleadingly named.

(3) THE DEFECT NEITHER OF US HAD: reporter would CHURN FOREVER on DC, never converging.
    inbound_fields._identity_of (:163) builds the canonical identity as
        'account_id': raw.get('accountId')
    reading ONLY accountId. Measured against the two real reporter shapes:
        Cloud {'accountId': '557058:abc', ...} -> {'display':'Cloud User','email':'c@x.com','account_id':'557058:abc'}
        DC    {'name':'dcuser', ...}           -> {'display':'DC User','email':'d@x.com','account_id':None}
    So on DC remote_acct is ALWAYS None. outbound_field_diff._diff_reporter (:105-111) then computes
    'desired' from the local reporter and emits changed['reporter'] whenever desired != remote_acct.
    For any RESOLVABLE reporter that comparison can never match, so the mutation is re-emitted on
    EVERY pass — even immediately after set_reporter succeeds, because the next snapshot still yields
    account_id=None. This is the same pathology as the pre-8b25 parent bug documented in
    dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent (~230 steady-state mutations of perpetual re-emission).

    That directly breaks THIS STORY'S OWN AC: 'an immediately repeated writing pass writes nothing
    (idempotence)'. So implementing set_reporter WITHOUT fixing _identity_of would turn a currently
    silent no-op into visible infinite churn — strictly worse, and it would fail the live idempotence
    test. _identity_of must also read DC's 'name' into the canonical identity.

VERDICT for the plan: set_reporter -> IMPLEMENT (DC {'name': ...} payload) + fix
inbound_fields._identity_of to carry DC's name, NO change to dispatch_apply_phases.py.
That is the third time this epic has produced the same shape: the obvious half-fix converts a silent
failure into a louder one without making the capability work.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SPIKE — set_parent on DC. MECHANISM IDENTIFIED (from the library + its docs); LIVE CONFIRMATION STILL
OUTSTANDING, and I am labelling which is which rather than blurring them.

WHAT IS PROVEN (introspected from the installed pycontribs/jira 3.10.5, the very library J6's
transport is built on):

  jira.JIRA.add_issues_to_epic(epic_id: str, issue_keys: str | list[str], ignore_epics=None) -> Response
      "Add the issues in issue_keys to the epic_id. Issues can only exist in one Epic!"

  jira.JIRA has NO 'parent' method and NO 'reporter' method at all (dir() scan of 189 public methods).

So on DC, EPIC membership is a distinct Greenhopper/Agile operation, NOT the fields.parent write that
Cloud uses. Cloud's set_parent (acli.py:678) PUTs {'fields':{'parent':{'key':...}}} to
/rest/api/3/issue/{key} and, on modern Cloud, that single field covers BOTH sub-task parents and epic
membership. DC has not converged those: fields.parent is sub-task-only; epics live behind Epic Link /
the Greenhopper endpoint the library wraps.

CONSEQUENCE: DC's set_parent must BRANCH on the parent's issue type — epic parent ->
add_issues_to_epic; sub-task parent -> raw PUT fields.parent. rebar models epics as ORDINARY parents
(dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent passes a bare parent_key with no type), so the transport has to
determine the parent's type itself. A naive fields.parent write for an epic parent is the failure the
plan predicted: it does not error, it just does not take — and then the differ re-emits the parent
mutation on every pass. That is the SAME churn signature as the pre-8b25 Cloud parent bug and as the
reporter churn resolved in the previous comment.

Also note the CLEAR path: Cloud clears with {'fields':{'parent':None}}. There is no
'remove_issues_from_epic' in the library — clearing an epic link on DC needs its own answer. Flagging,
not guessing.

WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN, and needs the harness:
  * that the harness image (Jira 8.17.1) has the Greenhopper/Agile endpoint enabled at all;
  * whether add_issues_to_epic wants the epic's numeric ID or its KEY (the signature says epic_id: str
    but that is not decisive);
  * how to CLEAR an epic link;
  * whether rebar's epic-typed parents round-trip through the inbound differ afterwards (the
    idempotence question, which is the one that actually matters for this story's AC).

I attempted the local harness twice; both times Cargo/Tomcat hard-timed-out (45 min,
'Deployable failed to finish deploying within the timeout period [2700000]') on a host running several
other containers. The CI job 'jira DC harness smoke' DOES bring it up successfully, so the live half of
this spike should run there.

VERDICT for the plan: set_parent -> IMPLEMENT WITH A TYPE BRANCH (add_issues_to_epic for epic parents,
fields.parent for sub-tasks), with the four open questions above resolved against the CI harness before
the implementation is trusted. It is no longer an open-ended 'spike first' — the mechanism is known and
the remaining unknowns are enumerated and testable.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CORRECTION — my triage table said three members had 'no library helper, use raw PUT'. That was WRONG,
and the plan is now library-first throughout.

WE DO USE pycontribs/jira DIRECTLY, and always have. Every method in the DC transport goes through it:
client.create_issue, .issue, .assign_issue, .transitions, .transition_issue, .search_issues,
.add_comment, .comments, .create_issue_link. There is NO hand-rolled REST in that file — the only
'requests' import is for exception TYPES (the SSLError-vs-ConnectionError classification from 9fd4).
Hand-rolling a rest_client.py was PR #120's approach, which this epic rejected.

MY ERROR: I enumerated jira.JIRA (189 public methods) and concluded set_parent/remove_label/
set_reporter had no helper. The library's API is SPLIT across jira.JIRA and jira.resources.Issue, and
Issue.update(fields=..., update=...) covers all three:
    set_parent (sub-task) -> issue.update(fields={'parent': {'key': ...}})
    remove_label          -> issue.update(update={'labels': [{'remove': ...}]})
    set_reporter          -> issue.update(fields={'reporter': {'name': ...}})
So ALL TWELVE are reachable through the library; none needs raw REST.

THIS IS THE SAME MISTAKE J6 SHIPPED AS A BUG, and our own code documents it. From add_label's
docstring (transport.py:273): 'add_field_value lives on the ISSUE resource, not on the client:
jira.JIRA has no such attribute (verified against jira 3.10.5), so the earlier client-level call raised
AttributeError on every invocation — this method could never have worked. It shipped because it had no
test at any tier.' I scanned the same half of the same API and reached the same wrong conclusion, in a
plan whose whole purpose is fixing that class of defect.

Two further refinements this surfaces:
 * get_comments and get_issue_by_rest are missing SURFACE, not missing capability — the transport
   ALREADY calls client.comments (:327) inside get_comment_map and client.issue (:234) inside
   get_issue. They are trivial exposures.
 * That weakens my earlier 'the library shaped our gaps' hypothesis. The library provides a helper for
   effectively all of them, so the gaps are not library-shaped — they are ORACLE-shaped. We implemented
   exactly the surface the contract suite and J6's ACs demanded and stopped. Which is the same root as
   [rebar:cc77-8120-bcc6-47e8]: nothing forced completeness.

The Approach now states the library-first rule AND warns about the JIRA-vs-Issue split explicitly, so
the next implementer does not repeat it a third time.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LOOP ITERATION 2. Review round 5: BLOCK with 2 findings. One I FIXED; one I am DISPUTING with
evidence, which is a first in five rounds — the previous four were all correct and I said so.

DISPUTED (G6). The finding says client.add_issue_property 'does not appear anywhere in the codebase
or resolve via the installed jira package'. The first clause is true and expected — it is what this
story ADDS. The second is false. Verified directly against the worktree venv:

    jira 3.10.5
    hasattr(jira.JIRA, 'add_issue_property') -> True
    signature: (self, issue: str, key: str, data) -> Response
    defined in: .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/jira/client.py
    body: url = self._get_url(f'issue/{issue}/properties/{key}'); return self._session.put(url, ...)

That is exactly the entity-property endpoint, routed through the library's authenticated resilient
session. I have not weakened the plan to accommodate the finding; I have added the file path and the
method body to the triage row so the claim is checkable FROM THE PLAN rather than requiring the
reviewer to resolve an installed package. If the finding recurs against that citation, the next
reader should re-run the three lines above before believing either of us.

FIXED (E2/F1). The set_reporter AC was disjunctive — 'asserted by a test that the call site IS OR IS
NOT reached'. That was stale: I resolved the upstream decision two comments ago and never tightened
the criterion. A test that passes either way enforces nothing. It is now definite, and split in two:
 * implement issue.update(fields={'reporter': {'name': ...}}) AND fix inbound_fields._identity_of to
   carry DC's name; dispatch_apply_phases.py is explicitly NOT modified;
 * reporter sync is proven IDEMPOTENT — after a successful write, the next differ pass emits NO
   reporter mutation. That is the criterion that fails today, and 'the write succeeded' does not
   satisfy it.

Also corrected a stale row in the failure-mode table: set_reporter was listed under 'propagates
(crashes)' from round 2's classification; it is not reached on DC at all today, so the crash bucket is
1 member (get_issue_by_rest), not 2.

Re-review running.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LOOP ITERATION 4. Review round 6: BLOCK, 2 findings — but both state the SAME defect, and it was
mine: inbound_fields.py is required by the triage AND by an explicit AC, yet was absent from the Scope
file list. An implementer following Scope would not have known to touch it, and the
reporter-idempotence AC cannot pass without it.

Cause: I added the _identity_of requirement to the triage and the ACs two rounds ago and never
propagated it to Scope. Same class as round 4's finding (Scope contradicting Approach). Scope is the
section I keep forgetting to update, which is worth naming as a personal failure mode rather than
treating as two unrelated slips.

FIXED:
 * Added src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py to Scope, with the reason (_identity_of
   at :163 reads accountId ONLY, so a DC reporter yields account_id=None and the mutation re-emits
   forever) and the note that it is a CORE module, not an adapter one — the reviewer hedged 'or a
   shared path', and the distinction matters because the shape is vendor-neutral and both adapters
   feed it.
 * Tightened dispatch_apply_phases.py from 'ONLY if the verdict goes that way' to an explicit
   NOT MODIFIED, since the verdict is now resolved. Leaving a conditional file in Scope after the
   condition is settled is an invitation to edit it.
 * Rewrote file_impact to match Scope exactly (8 paths), so the file-impact-coverage gate and the plan
   agree.

Round 6 also carried NO repeat of the disputed add_issue_property finding from round 5 — the citation
of the library source path and method body appears to have settled it, which is the outcome I wanted:
the claim is now checkable from the plan rather than requiring the reviewer to resolve an installed
package. Re-review running.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LOOP ITERATION 5. Review round 7: BLOCK with FOURTEEN findings (up from 2). They collapse to four
distinct issues; I verified every one in source before acting. Two are serious and I had missed them
entirely.

(A) THE EXCEPTION MODEL IS INCOMPATIBLE — the biggest finding in this story so far, and it is the SAME
    ROOT as the missing members. The DC transport raises jira.exceptions.JIRAError. Two CORE call
    sites catch only urllib.error.HTTPError, which is what Cloud's urllib transport raises:
      * dispatch_apply_phases.py:119 — 'except urllib.error.HTTPError' around client.set_reporter.
        Its own comment calls a 4xx 'the common case' and the handler exists to DEGRADE SOFTLY. A DC
        JIRAError does not match, so it escapes and breaks the whole update.
      * outbound_differ.py:138-141 — _safe_get_issue maps HTTPError.code == 404 to _DELETED. A DC
        JIRAError matches NEITHER handler, so a remotely-deleted issue is not classified as deleted
        AND the exception escapes. Deletion detection silently breaks on DC.
    The port declares no exception contract, so the core reaches for a transport-specific type;
    urllib.error.HTTPError sitting in a vendor-neutral core module is a Cloud leak. Fix at the ADAPTER
    boundary (translate JIRAError into the neutral types, carrying .code so 404->_DELETED still
    works) rather than teaching every call site a second vendor's exceptions.
    This also REVERSES my own change from iteration 4: I marked dispatch_apply_phases.py NOT MODIFIED
    on identity grounds. Identity genuinely needs no change there — but the EXCEPTION model does, so
    the file is back in scope for a different reason. I over-corrected on partial evidence.

(B) MY WRITING-MODE AC NAMED THE WRONG TEST. It claimed
    test_dc_reconcile_pass_raises_no_unhandled_exception 'passes for a WRITING mode', but that test
    hard-codes 'dry-run' at test_reconcile_pass.py:207. Since this story ALSO requires the oracle file
    to stay UNMODIFIED, the AC was self-contradictory. Fixed by pointing it at the two tests that
    already run bootstrap-strict (:226/:229 and :286) and already call _assert_no_unhandled_exception —
    the writing-mode coverage existed; I named the wrong test.

(C) add_issue_property DISPUTED A SECOND TIME — and I can now EXPLAIN the reviewer's false negative
    rather than just contradict it. The method is real at runtime, but it is decorated with
    @translate_resource_args, so a STATIC symbol resolver reads the decorator and not the def. Same
    class of false-negative as the Serena finding [rebar:dbf9-3fc8-625d-4730]. The plan now carries a
    one-line reproduction command and says explicitly: verify at runtime, not statically. That is a
    better answer than my round-5 rebuttal, which only asserted the method existed.

(D) set_parent's spike had no exit condition. Now a distinct fourth verdict category (SPIKE-GATED)
    with four questions answerable in ONE CI harness run and a pre-decided fallback, so it cannot
    become open-ended research.

Scope grew to 10 files and 17 ACs. That is large for one story, and it is worth someone deciding
whether the exception-contract work should be split out — I have NOT split it, because the halves must
land together anyway: implementing get_issue_by_rest without translation breaks deletion detection,
which is the same 'both halves or neither' logic that governed the 5f48 fix. Flagging the judgement
rather than making it silently.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LOOP ITERATION 7 — STORY SPLIT. Review round 8 returned 11 blocks (round 7 had 14). Two double-digit
rounds is not convergence, and reading them showed WHY: most were self-contradictions bred by one plan
carrying two concerns.

The clearest example, flagged three separate ways by round 8: my Approach said 'translate at the
adapter into the neutral types the core ALREADY handles' — which implies no core edits — while my
Scope listed dispatch_apply_phases.py and outbound_differ.py as modified, and an AC implied core catch
clauses change. All three cannot be true. That tension was structural, not a wording slip, so no
amount of rewording was going to settle it.

SPLIT: the exception contract is now [rebar:bb8c-8283-80c6-4052] (J10), which BLOCKS this story. J10
is small and self-contained — declare BackendHTTPError on the port SUBCLASSING urllib.error.HTTPError,
translate JIRAError in the DC transport. The subclass choice is what makes the contradiction vanish:
core catch clauses need NO change (a subclass matches the existing except), and Cloud is untouched,
which the brainstorm's decision 7 requires ('must not alter or replace the live-validated Cloud path').

ALSO FIXED HERE, from round 8's remaining real findings:
 * _identity_of's KEY is now SPECIFIED, not left open. The existing account_id key receives
   'accountId or name'. Round 8 correctly noted the idempotence AC depends on WHICH key, and I had
   only said 'carry the name'. Measured across all three shapes: {accountId}->'557058:abc' (Cloud
   unchanged), {name}->'dcuser' (DC fixed), {accountId,name}->'557058:abc' (accountId wins, Cloud does
   not regress). The priority is load-bearing and a test must pin it.
 * outbound_field_diff.py is now explicitly documented as NOT a patch site, with the reason — it has
   been flagged three times. Once _identity_of populates account_id, _diff_reporter's comparison
   converges with no edit. It is a DIFFERENT FILE from outbound_differ.py, which is J10's concern; the
   near-identical names are a genuine trap.

# J9 — Make the DC transport actually drive a writing reconcile pass

## Context / Problem

Story J7 [rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1] landed the DC backend's port conformance and made it reachable
through config, then drove it against a REAL Jira Data Center instance for the first time (GitHub
Actions run 30604756524). The writing path CRASHES:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

`--mode dry-run` passes; `--mode bootstrap-strict` exits 1. So epic e369's headline capability —
Jira Server/Data Center support — does not work yet, and the epic cannot honestly close without this.

Filed as [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5]; this story is its implementation.

## The root cause is a PORT defect, and the gap is TWELVE members

An AST audit over `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/*.py` — collecting every method invoked on a
`client`/`transport` receiver, diffed against `JiraDataCenterTransport`'s methods and against every
Protocol in `_backend.py` — measured the real gap:

**Called by the core, ABSENT from the DC transport (12):**
`delete_issue`, `delete_issue_link`, `get_comments`, `get_issue_by_rest`, `get_issue_links`,
`get_parent_map`, `remove_label`, `set_entity_property`, `set_issue_property`, `set_parent`,
`set_reporter`, `validate_assignee_exists`.

**Declared on NO Protocol in `_backend.py`: the same 12.**

**The dominant failure mode is SILENT DEGRADATION, not crashing** — which inverts the obvious framing
of this story. Classifying every call site by whether an enclosing `try` swallows `Exception`:

| behaviour | count | members |
|---|---|---|
| propagates (crashes) | 1 | `get_issue_by_rest` (`set_reporter` was in this bucket in an earlier draft — it is not reached on DC at all today, see below) |
| swallowed at EVERY site | 7 | `delete_issue_link`, `get_comments`, `get_issue_links`, `set_issue_property`, `set_parent`, `validate_assignee_exists`, `get_parent_map` (the last via `hasattr`, `fetcher.py:448`) |
| MIXED — crashes at some sites, swallowed at others | 3 | `delete_issue`, `remove_label`, `set_entity_property` |

So a DC deployment does not mostly crash: it mostly **appears to converge while quietly not syncing
comments, links, parents, issue properties, or validating assignees.** `set_entity_property` is
swallowed at 2 of its 3 sites and crashes at the third — which is the ONLY reason any of this was
discovered. The crash was the lucky case.

This has a direct consequence for the acceptance bar: "no `AttributeError`" is the WRONG criterion,
because it is already true at most sites and true for the wrong reason. Fixing only the crash would
produce a green live run with the silent gaps fully intact — a worse outcome than today, because the
green run would be taken as proof the capability works.

### Per-method triage is required — a blanket rule is wrong

Three of the twelve need a decision that "implement it like Cloud does" actively gets WRONG. Each was
verified in source, and they establish that this story is TRIAGE, not bulk translation:

* **`get_parent_map` — Cloud's implementation is NOT portable.** `acli_graph.py:180` uses
  `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with an opaque `nextPageToken` CURSOR, and its own docstring records
  (ticket 8b25, live-proven) that the legacy `/rest/api/3/search` is RETIRED with HTTP 410 and that
  **sending `startAt` is rejected with HTTP 400**. That endpoint and pagination model are Cloud-v3
  only. DC REST v2 has `POST /rest/api/2/search` with OFFSET paging (`startAt`/`maxResults`). So the
  Approach's "read each Cloud counterpart first" is actively misleading here: copying Cloud yields a
  404/400 against DC. This one needs a v2 offset-paged implementation written fresh.
* **`set_reporter` — RESOLVED by measurement, and the answer is three-part.** (a) The CALL SITE needs
  no change: `jira_account_id` returns whatever `external_id` the family stored, and since bug 5f48
  merged, DC identities are minted under provider `jira` keyed on the DC USERNAME. Measured —
  `jira_account_id('<identity-ticket-id>') -> 'dcuser'`, while bare username / display name / email
  all return `None`. So the seam is already vendor-neutral and hands back exactly what DC needs;
  `set_reporter` is CONDITIONALLY reachable (on tickets whose reporter is an identity id), not
  unreachable. (b) The TRANSPORT method is needed with a DC payload:
  `issue.update(fields={'reporter': {'name': …}})`. (c) **The defect neither the plan nor the review
  had:** `inbound_fields._identity_of` (:163) builds the canonical identity from `raw.get("accountId")`
  ONLY. Measured against both real shapes, a DC reporter yields `account_id=None` while display/email
  survive — so `_diff_reporter` (`outbound_field_diff.py:105-111`) re-emits `changed["reporter"]` on
  EVERY pass, even straight after a successful write, because the next snapshot still reads `None`.
  Implementing the transport method WITHOUT fixing `_identity_of` converts a silent no-op into visible
  infinite churn and fails this story's own idempotence AC.
* **`set_entity_property`** is the one with live evidence, and it is the story's spine — but note it
  is swallowed at 2 of its 3 sites, so fixing it does NOT make the other two observable.

### The exception model is SPLIT OUT to J10 — not this story's problem

The DC transport raises `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` while two CORE modules
(`dispatch_apply_phases.py:119`, `outbound_differ.py:138-141`) catch only `urllib.error.HTTPError`.
That is real and verified, and it is **[rebar:bb8c-8283-80c6-4052] (J10)**, which BLOCKS this story.

It lived here for two review rounds and produced double-digit findings largely from one tension: an
Approach saying "translate into types the core already handles" (implying no core edits) against a
Scope listing two core files. Separating the exception CONTRACT from the member IMPLEMENTATION lets
each be stated without contradicting the other. J10 lands first; this story then implements the
members on a transport whose error contract is already settled.

### The triage, DECIDED — verdict per member

Recorded here so the executor implements rather than researches. Each verdict is backed by the call
site and by DC REST **v2** (not Cloud v3). "IMPLEMENT" means a normal v2 call; the two hard cases are
called out explicitly.

| member | verdict | basis |
|---|---|---|
| `set_entity_property` | IMPLEMENT | `client.add_issue_property(issue, key, data)`. VERIFIED PRESENT at RUNTIME in jira 3.10.5. Reproduce THREE independent ways — (i) `grep -n 'def add_issue_property' .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/jira/client.py` → **line 2961**; (ii) `python -c "import jira,inspect; print(inspect.signature(jira.JIRA.add_issue_property))"`; (iii) `pip show jira` → 3.10.5 → `(self, issue: str, key: str, data) -> Response` in `jira/client.py`; body is `self._session.put(self._get_url(f"issue/{issue}/properties/{key}"), …)`. **A STATIC symbol lookup will NOT find it** — it is wrapped in `@translate_resource_args`, so a resolver reading the AST sees the decorator, not the `def`. Two review rounds reported it absent for this reason; the same class of false-negative as [rebar:dbf9-3fc8-625d-4730]. Verify at runtime, not statically. (It is correctly absent from OUR codebase — that is what this story adds.) Value must reach the API **verbatim** (Cloud bug 0b27: wrapping in `{"value": …}` silently stored the wrong shape) |
| `set_issue_property` | IMPLEMENT | same endpoint — Cloud's `set_entity_property` is literally an alias of it (`acli_rest.py:266`) |
| `delete_issue` | IMPLEMENT | `client.issue(key).delete()` |
| `delete_issue_link` | IMPLEMENT — **plus a call-site caveat** | `client.delete_issue_link(id)`. But `dispatch_one.py:733` catches `subprocess.CalledProcessError` and treats it as IDEMPOTENT SUCCESS (`_links_applied += 1`); its comment says outright "delete_issue_link shells out via ACLI (raises CalledProcessError, NOT an HTTPError)" — a Cloud/ACLI-specific handler. DC raises `BackendHTTPError` (post-J10), which does NOT match, so a concurrent-removal 404 would escape and unwind the pass instead of being absorbed. So each of the twelve needs a recorded verdict — IMPLEMENT (with the DC v2 shape, not Cloud's),
NOT-APPLICABLE (`NotImplementedError` naming the limitation), or UNREACHABLE-BY-CALL-SITE (with the

A METHODOLOGICAL NOTE, because it changed the answer twice: an audit that matches only
`client.method(...)` CALL forms under-counts, because the reconciler frequently passes the method as
a VALUE — `_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)` (`dispatch_one.py:731`),
`_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, ...)` (`dispatch_one.py:321`). The audit must collect
every ATTRIBUTE ACCESS on a `client`/`transport` receiver. A first pass using the narrow pattern
reported ten and missed `delete_issue_link` and `set_parent`; the corrected pass reports twelve.

All twelve ARE implemented for Cloud, spread across `adapters/jira/acli_rest.py`, `acli.py` and
`acli_graph.py`.

So `set_entity_property` is not "the" missing method — it is the FIRST one a live writing pass
happened to reach. Eleven more sit behind it. **Implementing only `set_entity_property` would move the
crash one call deeper** and produce another red run, looking like progress while the capability stays
broken.

`TicketTransport` declares six members (`create_issue`, `get_issue`, `update_issue`,
`transition_issue_by_name`, `add_label`, `search_issues`); the core reaches for twenty-one distinct
transport members. The port describes under a third of its own requirement. That is exactly why `isinstance` conformance, the backend contract suite,
and 1636 reconciler unit tests were all green against a transport that cannot complete a writing pass.
**Conformance to an incomplete port proves less than it appears to** — the same class as J6's
`add_label` defect, where the only oracle was a fake mirroring the author's assumption.

## Approach

1. TRIAGE each of the twelve to one of IMPLEMENT / NOT-APPLICABLE / UNREACHABLE-BY-CALL-SITE, with
   evidence (see the triage section above — `get_parent_map` and `set_reporter` both break the naive
   rule). Then implement the IMPLEMENT set **through pycontribs/jira**, which the DC transport already uses
   exclusively (no hand-rolled REST anywhere in it; the only `requests` import is for exception
   TYPES). Every one of the twelve is reachable via the library — but its API is SPLIT across
   `jira.JIRA` and `jira.resources.Issue`, and scanning only the former is exactly how J6 shipped the
   `add_label` defect (`add_field_value` lives on Issue, not the client) and how this plan's own first
   triage wrongly concluded three members had 'no helper'. `Issue.update(fields=…, update=…)` covers
   parent, reporter and label-removal. Read each Cloud counterpart for its CONTRACT, but do not assume
   its endpoint or pagination is portable — `set_entity_property` is
   Cloud's alias for `set_issue_property`, which PUTs to
   `/rest/api/3/issue/{key}/properties/{prop}` with the value sent **verbatim as the body** — an
   earlier Cloud bug (0b27) wrapped it in `{"value": ...}` and silently stored the wrong shape, so
   copy the corrected contract, not the intuition. DC is REST **v2**.
2. Where a method is genuinely not applicable to DC, it must raise a clear `NotImplementedError`
   naming the DC limitation — never be left absent to fail as `AttributeError` mid-pass. Each such
   decision needs evidence, not assumption.
3. Make absence detectable AT CONSTRUCTION rather than at some call site months later. `TicketTransport`
   is currently `class TicketTransport(Protocol)` with **no `@runtime_checkable`**, so
   `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` raises `TypeError` rather than returning `False` — verified
   directly, and it means the naive "just isinstance it" mechanism does not work. So: add
   `@runtime_checkable` to `TicketTransport` (matching `Backend` and the capability protocols, which
   already carry it), declare the required members on it, and assert conformance where a backend is
   BUILT — `_build_jira_datacenter_backend` in `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` and the Cloud
   equivalent — so a missing member fails loudly at construction.
4. Make the failures OBSERVABLE, by a named mechanism. **`transport.py` currently has NO logging at
   all** (zero `logging`/`logger` references — verified), which is precisely why a failure in a
   swallowed member surfaces nothing. Add the module-level convention its sibling adapters already
   use — `import logging` + `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`, exactly as
   `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:13,25` does — and have each newly-implemented member log at
   WARNING naming the MEMBER and the REMOTE ID before the error propagates (J10 has already
   translated it to `BackendHTTPError` by then).
   **Use the logger, not `alert_store`:** `alert_store.append(record, repo_root)` requires a
   `repo_root` the transport does not have and should not acquire — the transport is a vendor
   adapter, not a store client. Sibling adapters use `logger.warning` for exactly this class of
   event (`acli_cli_ops.py:415`, `acli_subprocess.py:135,140`, `jira_family/sanitizers.py:85`), so
   this follows the established convention rather than inventing a second one.
5. Add a STRUCTURAL TEST that every transport member the core reaches for is declared on the port.
   It must collect EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver, not just call forms:
   a call-form-only audit silently under-counts (see the methodological note below) and would let the
   thirteenth member slip in unnoticed. This is what stops the class of defect recurring on the next
   backend.

**Alternative rejected:** implement `set_entity_property` alone. It fixes one crash, leaves eleven,
and leaves the port still misdescribing what the core needs.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — ALSO gains a
  module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (it has none today) so member failures are
  observable; see Approach step 4. And implement (or
  explicitly `NotImplementedError`) the ELEVEN unguarded absentees listed in the audit above, plus a
  deliberate decision on `get_parent_map`. **NOT just `set_entity_property`** — implementing one
  method moves the crash one call deeper and produces another red live run.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — add `@runtime_checkable` to `TicketTransport`
  (it currently lacks it, so `isinstance` against it raises `TypeError`) and declare the members the
  core actually requires.
- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py`** — `_identity_of` (:163) currently builds
  the canonical identity from `raw.get("accountId")` ONLY, so a DC reporter yields `account_id=None`
  and the reporter mutation re-emits on every pass.
  **THE KEY IS SPECIFIED, not left open:** the existing `account_id` key receives
  `raw.get("accountId") or raw.get("name")`. Not a new key — `_diff_reporter` reads `account_id`, so
  putting DC's `name` anywhere else leaves the comparison broken. PRIORITY IS LOAD-BEARING:
  `accountId` must win. Measured across all three payload shapes —
  `{accountId}` → `'557058:abc'` (Cloud unchanged); `{name}` → `'dcuser'` (DC fixed);
  `{accountId, name}` → `'557058:abc'` (Cloud does NOT regress). Reversing that order silently
  re-identifies every Cloud user, so a test must pin it.
  This is a CORE module both adapters feed, which is why the precedence is stated here rather than
  left to the implementer.
- **`outbound_field_diff.py` is NOT a patch site** — stated explicitly because it has been raised
  three times. `_diff_reporter` (:105) reads `reporter_identity.get("account_id")`; once `_identity_of`
  populates that key on DC, `desired` and `remote_acct` both become `'dcuser'` and the comparison
  converges with NO edit to this file. Do not confuse it with `outbound_differ.py` (a different file,
  and J10's concern).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` and
  `adapters/jira/backend.py` — assert transport conformance in the FACTORY, where the backend is
  built, so a missing member fails loudly at construction rather than at a call site later.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` — `FakeTransport` gains whatever members the
  widened port declares, since it is the contract suite's stand-in and must satisfy it.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — a structural test for the audit: every transport attribute the
  core reaches for is declared on the Protocol.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — already written by J7; it is the oracle and
  must go from FAIL to PASS unmodified. **Do not weaken it to accommodate the fix.**

## Testing

- unit: each implemented method issues the right REST call, asserted against a fake client. For
  `set_entity_property` this includes
  that the property KEY and VALUE reach the endpoint intact, since a silently wrong shape breaks
  correlation without raising.
- structural: the core-call-sites-vs-Protocol audit is a TEST, not a one-off grep, so a future core
  module reaching for an undeclared transport method fails CI. Give it teeth with a synthetic case,
  mirroring `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py::test_checker_flags_a_synthetic_violation`.
- live: J7's `test_reconcile_pass.py` must pass in the `jira-dc-harness` CI job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ALL TWELVE absent members carry a RECORDED VERDICT — implemented, `NotImplementedError` naming
      the DC limitation, or documented as unreachable-by-call-site with the upstream decision named —
      never simply absent: `delete_issue`, `delete_issue_link`, `get_comments`, `get_issue_by_rest`,
      `get_issue_links`, `get_parent_map`, `remove_label`, `set_entity_property`,
      `set_issue_property`, `set_parent`, `set_reporter`, `validate_assignee_exists`
- [ ] the acceptance bar is NOT "no `AttributeError`". For each of the SEVEN members whose call sites
      swallow `Exception` at every site, and the THREE mixed ones, a test asserts the member is
      actually PRESENT on the transport — because absence at those sites produces silent degradation,
      so "the pass converged" and "no exception escaped" are both true today while nothing works
- [ ] a test asserts a DC transport with a member REMOVED is rejected at construction (not at a later
      call site), proving the guard fires
- [ ] `get_parent_map` is implemented against DC REST **v2** offset pagination
      (`POST /rest/api/2/search`, `startAt`/`maxResults`) or explicitly declined — NOT copied from
      Cloud, whose `/rest/api/3/search/jql` cursor endpoint rejects `startAt` with HTTP 400 and does
      not exist on DC
- [ ] `set_reporter` is implemented on the DC transport as
      `issue.update(fields={"reporter": {"name": …}})`, AND `inbound_fields._identity_of` carries
      DC's `name` into the canonical identity. `dispatch_apply_phases.py` is NOT modified — the
      identity seam already returns the DC username
- [ ] reporter sync is proven IDEMPOTENT on DC: a test asserts that after a successful reporter
      write, the next differ pass emits NO reporter mutation. This is the criterion that fails today
      and that `_identity_of` alone fixes — it is not satisfied by "the write succeeded"
- [ ] `set_entity_property` specifically is implemented and unit-tested, with the test asserting the
      property key and value reach the REST layer INTACT — Cloud bug 0b27 stored `{"value": x}`
      instead of `x`, and a wrong shape breaks correlation WITHOUT raising, so "it did not error" is
      not evidence here
- [ ] `TicketTransport` is made `@runtime_checkable` and declares the members the core requires —
      without that decorator `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` raises `TypeError` rather than
      returning `False` (verified), so the construction-time guard cannot work at all as a bare
      isinstance check
- [ ] the conformance assertion runs where a backend is BUILT (`_build_jira_datacenter_backend` and
      the Cloud equivalent), so a missing member is a loud construction failure
- [ ] a structural test asserts every transport member the core reaches for is declared on the port,
      collecting EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver — not just `client.x(...)`
      call forms, since a call-form-only audit silently under-counts (it missed `delete_issue_link`
      and `set_parent` here). Proven to FIRE on a synthetic undeclared member
- [ ] [operator-attested] a full writing reconcile pass (`bootstrap-strict`) against the J5 harness
      converges with no unhandled exception. **The covering tests are
      `test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` (test_reconcile_pass.py:226,229) and
      `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` (:286)** — both already run
      `bootstrap-strict` and both call `_assert_no_unhandled_exception`.
      NOT `test_dc_reconcile_pass_raises_no_unhandled_exception`, which hard-codes `dry-run` at :207.
      An earlier draft of this AC named that test and was self-contradictory, since this story also
      requires the oracle file to stay UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] [operator-attested] an immediately repeated writing pass writes nothing (idempotence) —
      J7's `test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` passes
- [ ] [operator-attested] a DC-created ticket carries `creation_channel == 'jira'` — J7's
      `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` passes
- [ ] a failure in ANY newly-implemented transport member is OBSERVABLE — logged at WARNING+ naming
      the member and the remote id — and a TEST PROVES THE LOGGER FIRES, using pytest's `caplog` to
      assert the record is emitted and carries both the member name and the remote id when the
      underlying call raises. An observability requirement with no test asserting emission is exactly
      the "absence of errors is not evidence" trap this criterion exists to close. This is not
      optional polish: SEVEN
      of the twelve have call sites that swallow `Exception` at EVERY invocation, and they stay
      swallowed after implementation. Without this, J9 ships the exact defect class it exists to fix —
      a DC write that fails and reports nothing
- [ ] `validate_assignee_exists` is tested on its ERROR path, not just its happy path: a definitive
      miss raises `AssigneeNotFoundError` SPECIFICALLY (the type already defined at
      `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:43`). `outbound_assignee.py:113` branches on
      `type(exc).__name__ == "AssigneeNotFoundError"`, so any other exception type silently downgrades
      every DC assignee resolution to the non-authoritative string-match fallback — "a lookup
      happened" is not evidence
- [ ] the oracle is not adjusted to FIT the fix. Stated as a property, because the original form
      ("`git diff` shows `test_reconcile_pass.py` unchanged") encoded a premise that proved FALSE:
      that file's writing-mode assertions called `_envelope()`, which asserts a JSON envelope the
      reconciler never emits in a writing mode (`__main__.py:444-452` — ONLY the `no_write` branch
      calls `json.dumps`; line 444's own comment says "Writing-mode output shape is unchanged (OK
      line on stdout, no JSON)"). Those assertions could NEVER have passed; the defect was masked
      because the pass crashed on the missing `set_entity_property` first. An AC that forbids
      touching a file cannot survive that file containing a bug, so the criterion is now the three
      properties that actually distinguish a corrected oracle from a weakened one, EACH verifiable
      by reading the diff:
      (a) no writing-mode assertion is DELETED without a replacement that still fails when the
          reconciler misbehaves — `_assert_wrote_nothing` reads the program's own convergence
          verdict, which `__main__.py:455` prints exactly when `computed == 0 and applied == 0`;
      (b) assertions on modes that DO emit an envelope are retained unweakened — the `dry-run` test
          still calls `_envelope()` and still asserts `mutation_failures == 0`;
      (c) every changed assertion cites the emitting code that justifies the new shape, and the
          citation is checked against that code rather than taken on trust
